skill.name: newsletter-curation
skill.description: Guide for planning and curating email newsletters. It covers newsletter formats, issue structure, content sourcing, commentary writing, sending cadence, subject lines, growth tactics, and performance metrics.
skill.summary: Create curated newsletter issues with source research, editorial structure, commentary, cadence, and growth guidance.
skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: Most backtick-related static findings are false positives from Markdown fences and inline formatting. The remote installer command on SKILL.md line 14 is a confirmed critical pipe-to-shell risk, and several infsh command examples create real external service exposure.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl piped to sh with separate download, checksum verification, and an explicit user-run install command.

remediation.issue: The skill grants broad Bash(infsh *) permission.
remediation.suggestion: Narrow the allowed command scope or require explicit confirmation before sending content to inference.sh apps.

remediation.issue: The social posting example can publish externally.
remediation.suggestion: Require final user review and approval before any command that posts to social platforms.

remediation.issue: Executable examples are mixed with writing templates.
remediation.suggestion: Separate shell commands from non-executable examples and label commands that contact external services.

content.value_statement: Teams need a repeatable way to turn scattered sources into useful newsletter issues. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan formats, source topics, write commentary, and improve growth habits.
actual_capabilities: Suggests newsletter formats such as link roundups, essays, interviews, and data trend issues.
Provides issue structures for introductions, big stories, curated links, quick hits, and community items.
Shows search prompts for finding news, research, discussions, and deep analysis through inference.sh apps.
Guides commentary writing with a formula for context, reader value, and editorial perspective.
Recommends cadence, subject line patterns, growth tactics, and performance metrics.
limitations: Requires user review before publishing or posting any generated content.
External search and social posting examples depend on inference.sh apps and account access.
Does not verify source accuracy beyond sources supplied or searched during the session.
Does not manage subscriber lists, send campaigns, or track analytics directly.

use_cases.title: Plan a Weekly Industry Digest
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable issue structure with curated links, short commentary, and a consistent send schedule.

use_cases.title: Develop a Creator Newsletter
use_cases.description: Turn personal expertise into a focused issue with an essay, selected links, and a clear reader call to action.

use_cases.title: Standardize Editorial Curation
use_cases.description: Create source filters, commentary rules, subject line patterns, and quality checks for a team newsletter.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Link Roundup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a weekly link roundup for [audience] about [topic]. Include five source slots, a short introduction, commentary prompts, and a clear closing call to action.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full Weekly Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan issue #[number] for [newsletter name]. Include a big story, worth reading section, quick hits, stat of the week, subject lines, and a send cadence recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Curated Commentary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these candidate sources for [audience]. Select the strongest items, explain why each matters, and write concise commentary with my editorial point of view.

prompt_templates.title: Design Growth and Measurement
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a six-week newsletter growth plan for [newsletter]. Include distribution channels, referral ideas, archive strategy, engagement prompts, and metrics to monitor after each issue.

output_examples.input: A weekly AI newsletter for product managers needs a clear issue structure.
output: Opening note: two sentences on the week in AI product work.
Big story: one launch or policy change with practical product impact.
Worth reading: five curated links with short editorial commentary.
Quick hits: three brief updates for scanning readers.
Closing: one question that invites replies from subscribers.

output_examples.input: A founder wants better commentary for a link about pricing research.
output_examples.output: This piece matters because it connects pricing experiments to customer trust. I would highlight the research method, the strongest finding, and one practical test readers can run this week.

output_examples.input: An editorial team needs subject line ideas for a developer tools digest.
output: #18: The build tool shift hiding in plain sight
5 developer tools worth testing this week
This week in dev tools: faster builds, fewer tabs
The migration guide teams keep asking for

best_practices: Verify each source before writing commentary or recommending it to readers.
Keep each issue focused on the reader value promised by the subject line.
Use a consistent send cadence and review performance after every issue.
anti_patterns: Sending long lists of links without editorial context.
Publishing AI-written summaries without checking source accuracy.
Running external posting commands before the user approves final copy.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create curated email newsletter issues, link roundups, commentary sections, subject lines, and growth plans.

faq.question: Can it find current sources?
faq.answer: It includes example prompts for external search apps. Current source gathering depends on available tools and user approval.

faq.question: Does it send email campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan and draft newsletter content, but it does not manage lists or send campaigns.

faq.question: Can it help with subscriber growth?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides growth tactics such as cross-promotion, social distribution, referral programs, archives, and lead magnets.

faq.question: Is external publishing automatic?
faq.answer: No. Any social posting or external publishing command should require final user review and explicit approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
